finding: The drill direction is correct, but its connector overlaps the track/body region and needs a canonical mount geometry check.
The boom is mostly hidden by the cab and wheels under current assembleParts layering; the ball sits inside the wheel envelope.
The v10 engine and siren are readable, but their outline/highlight treatment still needs gold-style approval.
The active individual track art occupies the body region instead of sitting below the chassis in the current runtime path.
One part contains two complete skis; it reads as a preassembled pair and conflicts with the single-module system.
The hover unit fits geometrically but its glossy purple material and contour system do not match the v9 vehicle.
The set assembles, but the propeller is front/three-quarter view and the complete batch has a different outline and highlight language.
The fuselage and pilot cabin point left while the runtime propulsion placement assumes a right-facing vehicle.
The canopy and seat are perspective-baked and the seat is not a strict side-view cab module.
The seaplane nose points left while the propeller is placed on the right, producing a physically contradictory vehicle.
